steps.title: Problem Identification
steps.desc:
I begin every project by observing on-site workflows and identifying stakeholders' pain points.
I document inefficiencies in data, processes, and user experience to clearly define:
"Exactly what problem needs to be solved?"

steps.title: Hypothesis & Structuring
steps.desc:
Rather than simply listing problems,
I reinterpret them through a cause-process-outcome framework to create testable hypotheses.
At this stage, I integrate clinical insights, data patterns, and operational constraints
to set realistic directions and goals.

steps.title: Solution Design & Execution
steps.desc:
Based on project objectives, I design integrated solutions including:

• Clinical trial operations and data flow architecture
• User experience-focused digital interfaces
• AI/automation model design and implementation
• Organizational collaboration and communication workflows
• Process optimization and error prevention systems

The key is creating structures that actually work in real-world settings,
not just theoretical ideas.

steps.title: Impact Validation
steps.desc:
I validate solution effectiveness through data-driven evaluation and derive improvements based on quantitative and qualitative assessments.

• Statistics and metrics-based analysis
• User, patient, and clinician feedback
• Process stability evaluation
• Reproducibility and scalability review

The goal is not just to "complete" a project,
but to create lasting value for the organization.

innovation.label: Featured Innovation
innovation.title: Generative AI-based Cognitive Intervention Framework
innovation.description: The 'Hwiwasoo' project, co-founded with a PhD student in Applied Physics at Hokkaido University to address cognitive decline and digital exclusion in older adults. It implements a triple-agent (Coach-Teacher-Companion) system to create a Context-Adaptive Cognitive Flow in daily life, maximizing user engagement.

items.title: AI-driven cognitive telerehabilitation for stroke: a randomized controlled trial
items.summary:
In a recent multicenter randomized controlled trial, AI-based cognitive telerehabilitation showed equivalent efficacy to traditional therapist-supervised cognitive rehabilitation.

63 stroke patients in the subacute phase (within 6 months) were randomly assigned to two groups for a total of 24 sessions over 6 weeks. Both groups showed significant improvements in key cognitive indicators (K-MMSE2, TMT, Digit Span).

Unsupervised **AI self-operated telerehabilitation demonstrated non-inferiority** compared to the therapist-led group, with high usability satisfaction.

These results suggest that AI cognitive rehabilitation platforms allowing real-time personalization and remote monitoring provide clinical value on par with conventional treatments.

items.title: A Generative AI Framework for Cognitive Intervention in Older Adults: An Integrated Engineering Design and Clinical Protocol
items.summary:
Digital exclusion and technology anxiety remain significant barriers to the practical application of cognitive interventions for the elderly. This clinical protocol paper proposes a multi-agent generative AI framework with a Coach–Teacher–Companion (CTC) structure to address these limitations.

The framework is designed to naturally integrate cognitive training into daily life and provide simultaneous cognitive, behavioral, and emotional support through adaptive difficulty adjustment and emotional monitoring. It systematically presents methodological and ethical safeguards for clinical application, including assessments for digital literacy (MDPQ-16), technology anxiety (CARS), and emotional safety (PANAS).

Designed to evaluate **usability (SUS), user experience (UEQ-S), adherence, emotional stability, and key cognitive indicators (MMSE, TMT, Digit Span)** through a 6-week pilot feasibility study protocol (n=14), this study provide initial evidence for the structural feasibility of clinical application of generative AI-based cognitive intervention for the elderly.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Mobile Telerehabilitation for Individuals with Cognitive Impairment: A Feasibility Study
items.summary:
This preliminary study evaluates the clinical feasibility and usability of AI-based mobile cognitive telerehabilitation. 13 participants, including stroke patients and older adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), underwent a 6-week, 24-session AI self-operated cognitive rehabilitation program.

MMSE scores improved significantly compared to pre-intervention, with overall improvement trends in Digit Span and Trail Making Test. While product quality and satisfaction were high in the overall usability assessment, the 'tolerance for error' domain was relatively low, highlighting the need for UI/UX improvements considering the elderly and digitally vulnerable populations.

This study shows that AI-based cognitive telerehabilitation, feasible without constant therapist intervention, is safe and practicable in real clinical environments and has potential effects on cognitive function improvement. It is significant in presenting the importance of usability-centered design amidst the expansion of digital therapeutics and telerehabilitation.
